topics.title: Fields & waves
topics.question: How does a field become a wave?
topics.description: Maxwell’s equations, polarization, interference, and diffraction. Building a picture of light before following its equations.
topics.prerequisites: Vector calculus and basic differential equations.
outline: Gradient, divergence, curl, and the integral theorems
Maxwell’s equations: local rules, global consequences
Plane waves, polarization, and Jones calculus
Interference, diffraction, and optical resolution

notebooks.Electromagnetic Pieces: The pieces that fit together into electromagnetism.
notebooks.Maxwell's Equations: A handwritten starting point for the laws of the field.

topics.title: Light & matter
topics.question: What does light see inside a material?
topics.description: From a driven electron to the collective response of a crystal. Connecting microscopic motion to the optical properties we measure.
topics.prerequisites: Classical waves and introductory quantum mechanics.
outline: The oscillator picture of material response
Linear susceptibility and dielectric response
Crystal structure, periodicity, and reciprocal space
Electrons in crystals and the origin of bands

notebooks.Crystal: A first look at periodic structure.
notebooks.Electrons in Crystals: Following electrons through a periodic material.
notebooks.Oscillator Model: Material response through the picture of a driven oscillator.

topics.title: Quantum optics
topics.question: What changes when light comes in quanta?
topics.description: Photons, optical states, and light–atom interactions. A route from field quadratures to the surprises of quantum light.
outline: Modes, creation and annihilation operators
Coherent and squeezed states; phase-space pictures
Two-level atoms, Rabi oscillations, and spontaneous emission
Photodetection, homodyne measurement, and coherence

topics.title: Open quantum systems
topics.question: Where does quantum information go?
topics.description: Dissipation, noise, measurement, and memory. Understanding the environment as part of the physics, rather than an afterthought.
outline: Density operators, quantum operations, and measurement
Markovian master equations and the Lindblad picture
Damped oscillators, thermal baths, and decoherence
Correlation functions and resonance fluorescence
Beyond the Markov approximation; diagrammatic approaches

topics.title: Quantum networks
topics.question: How do small quantum systems become a network?
topics.description: Inputs, outputs, and connections. Thinking about cavities, waveguides, and feedback as pieces of a larger dynamical system.
topics.prerequisites: Open quantum systems and linear systems.
outline: Input–output relations and scattering
The SLH description and composition rules
Cascaded systems and coherent feedback
Propagation, loss, and non-vacuum inputs

topics.title: Quantum information
topics.question: What can a quantum state tell us?
topics.description: Information, distinguishability, and estimation. Connecting abstract bounds to the measurements that make them meaningful.
topics.prerequisites: Linear algebra, probability, and quantum states.
outline: Channels, distinguishability, and the no-cloning theorem
Gaussian states, covariance matrices, and symplectic maps
Entanglement, squeezing, and noisy channels
Fisher information and parameter estimation

topics.title: Nonlinear & fiber optics
topics.question: When does light reshape itself?
topics.description: Frequency conversion, dispersion, and nonlinear propagation. Following energy and phase through media that respond to the field.
topics.prerequisites: Waves, material response, and optical modes.
outline: Nonlinear susceptibility and coupled-wave pictures
Second-harmonic generation, SPDC, and phase matching
Fiber modes, dispersion, and pulse propagation
Self-phase modulation, four-wave mixing, and solitons

topics.title: Learning & reservoirs
topics.question: Can a physical system learn from its own memory?
topics.description: Dynamical systems as information processors. The meeting point of quantum physics, temporal learning, and physical computation.
topics.prerequisites: Dynamics, probability, and basic machine learning.
outline: Linear readouts and temporal learning
Reservoir dynamics and fading memory
Quantum reservoirs and delayed feedback
Measurement, noise, and computational performance

topics.title: Mathematical methods
topics.question: Which mathematical picture makes the physics clearer?
topics.description: The tools behind the ideas: linear algebra, transforms, stochastic calculus, and approximation. Mathematics with a physical purpose.
outline: Eigenvectors, singular values, and changes of basis
Fourier pictures, spectra, and correlation functions
Perturbation theory and useful approximations
Stochastic equations and quantum noise

Crystal.start: Why study a material through its absorption spectrum?
Crystal.explains: How fields, geometry, and confinement change the optical response; then how lattice vectors, a basis, primitive cells, and reciprocal space describe a solid.
Crystal.connect: Continue with Electrons in Crystals to connect atomic structure to bands.

Electrons in Crystals.explains: Use the atomic picture as a starting point for understanding electron states and band structure in a crystal.

Electromagnetic Pieces.start: Build the physical and mathematical pieces before assembling Maxwell’s equations.
Electromagnetic Pieces.explains: Electric and magnetic fields, the meaning of the vacuum constants, material sources, and the intuition behind divergence, curl, Gauss’s theorem, and Stokes’s theorem.

Maxwell's Equations.start: Ask how light interacts with matter on the macroscopic scale.
Maxwell's Equations.explains: Read the equations as statements about sources and changes: charge, current, changing fields, and the connection to charge continuity.
